name: Ninh Binh food guide
summary: Ninh Bình eats mountain goat and crisp cơm cháy on the roads out to the karst, pork-ball noodles and nhệch salad on the Kim Sơn coast, and ant-egg sticky rice in Nho Quan when February comes.
body: Start with goat. Every road and lane out to Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính has dê núi shops, and the meat is firm because the animals climb the limestone. Order it rare with lime, wrapped in sung leaf and dipped in soy sauce, then break a cake of cơm cháy into the goat sauce.

Further out, the menu follows the district. Kim Sơn has bún mọc with fist-sized pork balls and gỏi nhệch, Vân Long grills its snakehead by the wetland, Gia Viễn makes shrimp paste and grills fish with straw, Yên Mô sells nem chua, giò trứng, and bánh đúc, and Nho Quan has forest honey, golden camellia tea, and Mường jar wine.

For a sit-down meal, the province lists its tourism restaurants and its cơm văn phòng set-rice rooms with addresses and phone numbers. Set rice starts from 30,000 đồng a portion where a room lists a price.
specialtiesLead: These are the plates to look for, with the district each one belongs to.

sections.heading: Named dishes
paragraphs: Goat sits on the valley roads, noodles and fish on the Kim Sơn coast, snails and fish in Gia Viễn and Vân Long, and teas, honey, and jar wine up in Nho Quan. The last few are OCOP products, the certified local goods to carry home.

spots.name: De tai chanh
spots.address: Roads toward Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính
spots.note: Rare goat dressed with lime, eaten wrapped in a sung leaf and dipped in soy sauce. Mountain goat here is firm, because the animals climb the limestone.

spots.name: De xao sa ot
spots.address: Roads toward Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính
spots.note: Mountain goat stir-fried with lemongrass and chili, one of the plates in the goat shops on the roads to the sights.

spots.name: De nui nhung me
spots.address: Roads toward Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính
spots.note: Mountain goat dipped in mẻ, fermented rice, at the goat tables on the roads to the sights.

spots.name: De nuong ngu vi
spots.address: Roads toward Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính
spots.note: Mountain goat grilled with five-spice.

spots.name: De ham thuoc bac
spots.address: Roads toward Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính
spots.note: Mountain goat stewed with Chinese medicinal herbs.

spots.name: Doi de chien
spots.address: Roads toward Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính
spots.note: Fried goat sausage, served with the other mountain-goat plates.

spots.name: Com chay sot de
spots.address: Roads toward Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính
spots.note: Ninh Bình’s crisp rice cake eaten with goat sauce, where the province’s two best-known foods meet on one plate.

spots.name: Chao thit de
spots.address: Roads toward Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính
spots.note: Rice porridge cooked with goat meat, from the same mountain-goat menu as the grills and stews.

spots.name: De u trau
spots.address: Roads toward Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính
spots.note: Goat cooked in rice husks.

spots.name: Ca ri de
spots.address: Roads toward Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính
spots.note: Goat curry from the mountain-goat menu.

spots.name: Goi ca nhech
spots.note: A salad of nhệch, the home dish of the Kim Sơn coast. Visitors also eat it in the old capital at Hoa Lư.

spots.name: Bun moc Kim Son
spots.note: Rice noodles in broth with pork balls the size of a child’s fist, made from leg meat seasoned with fish sauce and pepper and boiled on banana leaf. Eat it with banana flower, tía tô, rau răm, lime, and chili vinegar.

spots.name: Ca chuoi nuong
spots.note: Grilled snakehead from the Vân Long wetland, with white flesh, eaten with peanuts and herbs and dipped in fish sauce.

spots.name: Ca tre nuong
spots.note: Grilled catfish, one of the foods that draws visitors to the Vân Long wetland.

spots.name: Oc nui
spots.address: The limestone hills, April to August
spots.note: Snails that live in the limestone crevices and feed on forest leaves. Eat them from April to August, when the meat is thick.

spots.name: Xoi trung kien
spots.note: Sticky rice with brown-ant eggs from Nho Quan, made only in February. The eggs pop when you bite them.

spots.name: Nem chua Yen Mac
spots.note: Fermented pork seasoned with garlic, chili, đinh lăng leaf, and roasted rice powder. Yên Mô claims the same plate.

spots.name: Bun cha quat
spots.note: Rice noodles with grilled pork pressed into one wide, fan-shaped patty instead of small round pieces.

spots.name: Mien luon
spots.note: Glass noodles in a broth simmered from eel bones, topped with small eels cooked in seasoning and eaten with shredded banana flower.

spots.name: Banh xeo with nem lui
spots.note: A crisp rice pancake served with nem lụi, grilled pork skewers, and fresh herbs, the plate Ninh Bình orders after a day of sightseeing.

spots.name: Cua dong rang la lot
spots.note: Field crab fried with lá lốt, betel leaf.

spots.name: Banh da ca ro dong
spots.note: Rice cracker with field climbing perch, eaten with green mustard greens.

spots.name: Mam tep Gia Vien
spots.note: Shrimp paste from Gia Viễn, ranked among the province’s gifts to carry home.

spots.name: Ruou can Nho Quan
spots.note: Mường jar wine brewed from glutinous rice and yeast and never distilled. Add a little water to the jar and drink.

spots.name: Ruou Kim Son
spots.note: Kim Sơn’s local rượu, the liquor Ninh Bình names beside its goat and cơm cháy. It is a different drink from the Mường jar wine.

spots.name: Forest honey
spots.note: Wild forest honey from the Nho Quan uplands.

spots.name: Golden camellia tea
spots.note: Golden camellia tea, one of the Nho Quan mountain foods with forest honey and jar wine.

spots.name: Apple snails
spots.note: Apple snails, a Gia Viễn dish beside straw-grilled fish and shrimp paste.

spots.name: Straw-grilled fish
spots.note: Fish grilled with straw, a Gia Viễn dish beside apple snails and shrimp paste.

spots.name: Egg pork loaf
spots.note: Pork loaf made with egg, a Yên Mô specialty with bánh đúc and nem chua Yên Mạc.

spots.name: Banh duc
spots.note: Rice cake, a Yên Mô specialty with giò trứng and nem chua Yên Mạc.

spots.name: Chao chan gio
spots.note: Chạo made from pork hock, a Kim Sơn dish beside gỏi nhệch and bún mọc.

spots.name: Ca trau tien vua
spots.note: Snakehead once offered to the king, a Hoa Lư dish beside goat and cơm cháy.

spots.name: Ca ro Tong Truong
spots.note: Climbing perch from Tổng Trường, a Hoa Lư specialty beside goat and cơm cháy.

spots.name: Ca qua nau am
spots.note: Snakehead cooked the ám way, a Nho Quan dish.

spots.name: Pork with shrimp paste
spots.note: Pork cooked down with shrimp paste, sold as a certified OCOP product.

spots.name: Pennywort powder
spots.note: Dried pennywort powder, sold as a certified OCOP product.

spots.name: Ca ro floss
spots.note: Fish floss made from Tổng Trường climbing perch, sold as a certified OCOP product.

spots.name: Son kim cuc tea
spots.note: Tea brewed from sơn kim cúc, a small yellow mountain chrysanthemum, sold as a certified OCOP product.

spots.name: Vu Gia tea
spots.note: Vũ Gia tea, sold as a certified OCOP product beside sơn kim cúc tea and peach wine.

spots.name: Peach wine
spots.note: Peach wine, sold as a certified OCOP product beside the province’s two teas.

sections.heading: Themed dining
paragraphs: One food quarter and three craft villages: the noodle makers of Yên Ninh, the food village of Phong An, and the rượu village of Lai Thành.

seoTitle: Ninh Binh food guide — goat, com chay, and Kim Son noodles
seoDescription: Mountain goat and cơm cháy on the roads to the karst, Kim Sơn bún mọc, Nho Quan ant-egg sticky rice, and the tourism and set-rice restaurants of Ninh Bình.
